payload.title: Ledger export (export_snapshot) overwrites sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl from local view instead of merging by issue_id
payload.body:
LedgerService.export_snapshot (packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/knowledge/wiki/ledger/service.py:424) rebuilds sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl entirely from this session's local issues (self._all_issues(), itself a replay of this checkout's events.jsonl via _sync_best_effort) and writes it unconditionally through _write_snapshot_if_changed — there is no merge against the file already on disk, and no diff against the previously-committed snapshot other than byte-equality.

/sdd-done step 9.1 (.claude/commands/sdd-done.md:412-455) calls this export from a throwaway worktree and commits whatever comes out, then restores the main worktree's staged/working copy to match.

Failure mode: if a worktree's local ledger log is behind origin (e.g. built from an older origin/<base> before another concurrent session pushed new `ledger open`/`close` events — a known hazard per [[worktree-concurrent-sdd-worker]] and [[shared-checkout-branching-hazard]]), export_snapshot only knows about issues it has replayed locally. Running /sdd-done in that worktree regenerates issues.jsonl from an incomplete view and silently drops rows for issues opened/closed by the other session, overwriting the shared committed snapshot with a regression.

Suggested fix: export_snapshot should merge by issue_id against the existing committed sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl (union, keep rows present on disk that are absent from the local replay, let only genuinely superseded/compacted issue_ids be dropped) rather than treating the local view as authoritative — or /sdd-done should refuse the export (abort step 9.1) if the local ledger log's cursor lags origin for issues.jsonl's branch, rather than committing a shrinking diff unattended.

payload.title: Ledger export (export_snapshot) overwrites sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl instead of reconciling against the committed snapshot
payload.body:
Supersedes issue:1e13dd5b188b (closed: that issue's suggested fix — a flat row-level merge by issue_id — was insufficient and is replaced by this reconciliation design).

LedgerService.export_snapshot (packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/knowledge/wiki/ledger/service.py:424) rebuilds sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl entirely from this session's local issues (self._all_issues(), a replay of this checkout's local events.jsonl via _sync_best_effort) and writes it unconditionally through _write_snapshot_if_changed, with no reconciliation against the file already committed on disk.

/sdd-done step 9.1 (.claude/commands/sdd-done.md:412-455) calls this export from a throwaway worktree and commits whatever comes out.

Failure mode: if this checkout's local ledger event log never recorded issues opened/closed by another session/machine (events.jsonl is local, not itself git-synced — only the periodic issues.jsonl snapshot is committed), export_snapshot has no way to know about them and silently drops their rows from the shared committed snapshot. See [[worktree-concurrent-sdd-worker]] / [[shared-checkout-branching-hazard]] for the same class of concurrent-session hazard.

A flat JSON-row merge by issue_id against the committed file is NOT the right fix: issues.jsonl is a derived STATE snapshot, not raw events, so for any issue_id present in both local and committed versions there is no principled way to pick a winner from the snapshot alone (could produce duplicate issue_ids or resurrect an already-closed issue).

Correct fix — reconcile at export time, two-tier:
1. For issue_ids the local ledger log HAS seen (has at least one event for), the local derived state is authoritative (it legitimately includes any close/claim this session applied) — use it as-is.
2. For issue_ids present in the currently-committed sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl but absent from the local event log entirely, there is no local event to replay — carry those rows forward UNCHANGED into the new snapshot (do not drop them just because this session never saw them).
3. Only an issue_id with a local close/compaction event should actually disappear from the output.

Implementation sketch: before building new_content, read+parse the existing dest file (or the committed blob at HEAD if dest is mid-overwrite in a throwaway worktree), collect issue_ids with zero local events, and union their raw rows into `rows` prior to the sort — rather than attempting any kind of cross-machine event-log sync (there is no shared event transport to sync from).

payload.reason: Superseded by issue:62038221413a — the flat row-level JSON merge-by-issue_id this issue suggested is insufficient (issues.jsonl is a derived state snapshot, not raw events, so a naive merge could resurrect closed issues or produce conflicting duplicates). Replaced by a two-tier reconciliation design: local-authoritative for issue_ids the local event log has seen, carry-forward-unchanged for issue_ids known only to the committed snapshot.

export_snapshot now reconciles against the committed sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl: rows for issue_ids the local ledger has never recorded are carried forward unchanged, local state stays authoritative for known ids, locally compacted issues still drop; `wikitoolkit ledger export --no-reconcile` is the explicit destructive opt-out and /sdd-done §9.1 documents the invariant. Verified on the real ledger: 279 committed rows → 286 exported, 0 dropped (FEAT-671, TASK-4295/4296/4297, branch feat-FEAT-671-commands-sdd-done-fixes).

payload.title: Extract a programmatic build_wiki() from the wikitoolkit build click callback
payload.body:
The repository-scan build pipeline has no programmatic entry point: its logic lives inside the click callback `build` (packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/knowledge/wiki/cli.py:1560) and its nested `_pipeline()`. Every non-CLI caller must therefore shell out to the `wikitoolkit` console script (`parrot.knowledge.wiki.entry:main`, packages/ai-parrot/pyproject.toml:204).

Context: raised as brainstorm Option C and spec §8 Q2 of FEAT-672 (github-reviewer-local-repo-wiki), which needs to build a graph over a cloned repository from inside a long-lived aiohttp agent. FEAT-672 deliberately did NOT do this: the narrow `wikitoolkit build --storage-dir` flag it adds removes the blocking motivation, and extracting the pipeline is a wikitoolkit-core refactor with a far larger blast radius (vault mode, Roblox enrichment, language fingerprints, OKF export, graph.html, remote push all hang off that callback).

Remaining motivation, recorded so it is not lost: (1) the build cannot be tested end-to-end without spawning a process; (2) callers are coupled to the `wikitoolkit` script being resolvable on the host process's PATH/venv — a missing binary silently disables the feature; (3) error handling is exit-code granularity, and stdout is unusable as data because the navconfig banner precedes any output.

Suggested fix when a second in-process caller appears: lift `_pipeline()` into `build_wiki(root, config, *, force, no_export, no_graph, storage_dir, ...) -> BuildReport`, keep `wiki_write_lock` (project.py:76) inside it, and reduce the click callback to argument parsing plus a call. Do not do this speculatively — FEAT-672 is the only consumer today and it is served by the flag.

payload.title: executor _action_click text-contains path passes args to execute_script — breaks under Playwright/Page drivers
payload.body:
Where: packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/scraping/executor.py, _action_click (~line 449-516), the js_text_filter branch (click selector with `:-soup-contains(...)`).

What: it calls `await driver.execute_script(script, selector, js_text_filter)` with a script that reads `arguments[0]` / `arguments[1]`. PlaywrightDriver.execute_script (drivers/playwright_driver.py:265) and PageDriver.execute_script (drivers/page_driver.py:173) map to `self._page.evaluate(script, *args)`. Playwright's `page.evaluate(expression, arg=None)` accepts a single optional arg and has no `arguments` object, so the call raises TypeError (two positional args) / ReferenceError, and the click step fails. Only SeleniumDriver (execute_script with *args) works.

Why it matters: any catalogued browsing/scraping action that clicks by text-contains fails on the default Playwright/Obscura path used by WebBrowsingToolkit.

Suggested fix: build an IIFE expression with the selector and needle embedded via json.dumps and call `driver.evaluate(expr)` (portable: Playwright evaluates the expression; Selenium evaluate prepends `return`). Same pattern FEAT-681 adopts for the `submit` action. Add a test asserting execute_script is not called with extra args. Out of scope of FEAT-681 (sdd/specs/browsing-executor-action-gaps.spec.md §1 Non-Goals).

payload.title: executor _action_scroll bottom height_script starts with 'return' — SyntaxError under Playwright/Page drivers
payload.body: _action_scroll(direction='bottom') calls driver.execute_script('return Math.max(document.body.scrollHeight, ...)'). Selenium wraps scripts in a function body so 'return' is legal; PlaywrightDriver/PageDriver forward to page.evaluate(script), where a top-level 'return' is an 'Illegal return statement' SyntaxError, so scroll-to-bottom (lazy-load trigger) fails on those drivers. Fix: use driver.evaluate('Math.max(...)') (Selenium's evaluate prefixes return). Found while fixing issue:c10c1e94f4b3 (FEAT-682).

payload.title: planogram visual_features rule cannot require counts or specific poses: zone evidence prompt never sees the expected list
payload.body:
What: a `visual_features` rule binding (e.g. on a header zone) cannot express "two figures of Shaquille O'Neal" or "one with thumbs up, one with headphones and a game controller". Two causes:
1. `collect_rule_evidence` / `build_zone_prompt` (identification/evidence.py) asks the vision model to describe the zone crop NEUTRALLY. The binding's `params.expected` list is never sent, so the free description rarely mentions the specific cues. Real answer on epson_projector_not_backlit photo b1c7213b: ["EPSON logo", "Shaquille O'Neal promotional photos", "'Perfect for Business + Epic for Play' text", "Three black Epson projectors", "Feature bullet points banner"]. There is no pose and no count.
2. `visual_feature_match` (comparison/rules.py) counts an expected entry as matched when ANY of its keywords (or a substring) appears in the detected keywords. Entries that share a word (e.g. both containing "Shaquille") are indistinguishable, and quantities ("two") cannot be checked.

Effect: with expected ["Shaquille O'Neal", "thumbs up", "headphones", "game controller"] and threshold 1.0 the rule scored 0.25 and failed on a compliant poster. The config was reduced to ["Shaquille O'Neal"] (2026-10-15, planogram_id=16), so a poster missing one of the two figures now passes.

Suggested fix: add a verification mode to the zone evidence call. It would send the expected features as a closed checklist and ask for present/absent per item, with an optional count, e.g. {"feature": "Shaquille O'Neal", "min_count": 2}. Score per item from that answer instead of the keyword overlap. Keep the neutral mode as the default for back-compat.

payload.title: planogram fact_tag_present reports "price not legible" on legible fact tags (llm_detector run, no local OCR)
payload.body:
What: on epson_projector_not_backlit_planogram_config (planogram_id=16, product_on_shelves, perception_mode=llm_detector), the e2e run of 2026-10-15 on photo b1c7213b-8c49-4991-878e-d24426b52698-recap.jpg reported all 6 `fact_tag_present` bindings (price_required=true) as "fact tag present, price not legible". In the photo every tag shows a large readable price ($1499.99, $649.99, $999.99, $499.99, $549.99, $349.99).

Where: `_rule_fact_tag` (comparison/rules.py) finds the tag shapes, but `tag_price(tag_text(tag, perception.ocr_readings, reads))` returns None for each one.

Probable cause (not yet confirmed): the run had local_ocr=False, and the identification stage named 7 targets (6 projectors + the header), none of them a tag. So no tag has OCR text or an identification text to parse a price from. In llm_detector mode the tag shapes are detected but never read.

Impact: informative only. fact_tag_present is mandatory=false and never affects score or status, but the report is misleading for every llm_detector row with price_required tags.

Suggested fix: when price_required bindings exist and a tag has no text, read the tag crops, either through a batched tag-read vision call or by including tag shapes in identification. Alternatively, report "price not read" (unassessed) instead of a FAIL when no text source exists. Repro: the e2e runner with the candidate config, examples/planogram/images/epson_projector_not_backlit_planogram_config/.

payload.title: text_requirements can never match case-sensitive or punctuation-bearing requirements: _entity_texts lowercases every feature first
payload.body:
Where: packages/ai-parrot-pipelines/src/parrot_pipelines/planogram/comparison/rules.py, `_entity_texts` (return line: `[normalize_text(feature) for feature in features if feature]`), consumed by `_rule_text`.

What: every text feature (zone OCR, ROI content, identification text/product/evidence, zone visual_features phrases, registered facings) is passed through `normalize_text` (NFKC, lowercase, every non-alphanumeric char incl. `&` and `.` replaced by a space) BEFORE `TextMatcher.check_text_match`. TextMatcher already normalizes on its own for `contains`/ngram/auto, but its `regex`, `exact` and `case_sensitive=True` paths rely on the raw text, which never reaches them.

Consequence (verified 2026-10-15):
- `TextMatcher.check_text_match('Scan & Done', [normalize_text('Scan & Done.')], match_type='regex', case_sensitive=True).found` -> False (the feature is 'scan done').
- e2e run of epson_ecotank_planogram_config on both store photos: requirement `{required_text: 'EPSON', match_type: 'regex', case_sensitive: true}` FAILED ("missing mandatory text: EPSON") although the ROI/zone answers contain 'EPSON' verbatim ('EPSON Goodbye Cartridges. Hello Savings.').
- epson_scanner_backlit_planogram_config (planogram_id=1, dev DB) has a mandatory case-sensitive regex `Scan\s*&\s*Done`: that rule fails on every photo.
So `case_sensitive`, `regex` (with uppercase or punctuation) and `exact` with case are silently unusable in planogram rule_bindings.

Suggested fix: keep the raw features in `_entity_texts` (strip only the `ocr:` prefix handling TextMatcher already does) and let `TextMatcher` normalize per match_type; or pass both raw and normalized lists and choose per requirement (raw for regex / exact / case_sensitive, normalized for contains/auto). Must keep current behaviour for `contains` (case-insensitive, punctuation-insensitive) and the n-gram path. Tests: case-sensitive regex 'Scan\s*&\s*Done' matches 'Scan & Done.' and rejects 'scan & done'; 'EPSON' case-sensitive matches 'EPSON Goodbye...' and rejects 'Epson'; contains behaviour unchanged.

payload.reason: _entity_texts returns raw features; _rule_text prepares them per requirement (regex/exact raw, case-sensitive contains normalized keeping case, default unchanged). 10 tests.

payload.title: check_task_graph: let parallelism_notes suppress a possible-missing-dependency warning when it names the creating task
payload.body: check_graph() emits possible-missing-dependency whenever task B mentions a file that task A creates and B does not depend on A, even when the mention is prose-only (e.g. a "NOT in scope" list). The only way to silence a false positive today is to document it in parallelism_notes, which the checker ignores, so the warning is re-emitted on every run. Example: TASK-4334 in sdd/tasks/index/parrot-installer.json mentions parrot.sdd / parrot.sdd.scripts only in prose, and its parallelism_notes already explains why there is no edge to TASK-4070/4085, yet both warnings still fire. payload.title: parrot e2e up: detached daemon stops gracefully when the launcher exits normally (AC5 survival not met)
payload.body: Found by the real-subprocess scenario test_up_daemon_and_target_survive_launcher_exit (packages/ai-parrot-server/tests/e2e/test_up_detached_lifecycle.py, brief issue:792b6e2a8f25). `python -m parrot.e2e.cli up mcp-stdio` exits 0 with a ready RunState, but immediately afterwards the daemon (supervisor_identity) is gone and the persisted state is status=stopped, cleanup_complete=true, shutdown_forced=false, with no `down` call: a graceful stop (SIGTERM/SIGINT path in cli.py _run_daemon). payload.title: AuthorizingDataSource rewrites inner SQL in place while HTTP clones share entry.source across user managers
payload.body: Found by the FEAT-704 design-research seat (S2) and verified in source on 2026-10-19. packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/tools/dataset_manager/sources/authorizing.py:188-191 computes inject_rls_sql(self._inner.sql, ...) and assigns the rewritten SQL back to self._inner.sql, so RLS predicates accumulate on repeated requests and the mutation is visible to every holder of the same inner source. packages/ai-parrot-server/src/parrot/handlers/datasets.py:68-70 (_clone_agent_dm) builds per-user DatasetEntry clones with source=entry.source, i.e. the SAME source object is shared between user-scoped DatasetManagers, so one subject's RLS rewrite can leak into another subject's queries. Expected: RLS injection is request-scoped (operate on a per-call copy of the SQL/AST) and cloned entries deep-copy or re-instantiate their source. The semantic layer (FEAT-704) avoids both paths (per-request AST clone, DataFrame-only hand-off), but DatasetManager users remain exposed.

payload.title: navigator-session 1.0 (KeyRing) mismatch breaks parrot.security import — root cause of FEAT-562 M7 DatabaseAgent test errors + the §1 resolver blocker
payload.body: FEAT-562 TASK-3299 (M7) diagnosis: the DatabaseAgent/botmanager 'cannot import name DatabaseAgentToolkit' CI errors are NOT an independent bug. Real cause: parrot.security.credentials_utils imports 'KeyRing, VaultContext, open_sealed, seal' from navigator_session.vault (added by the vault-crypto-hardening feature, commit cd8690390 which pinned navigator-session>=1.0.0), but the resolvable/installed navigator_session is 0.10.0, which has no KeyRing. So 'import parrot.security' raises ImportError, cascading through parrot.tools -> parrot.bots.database -> the DatabaseAgent tests. This is the SAME external resolver blocker recorded in the FEAT-562 spec §1 addendum (navigator-session>=1.0.0 unresolvable on py3.13), but with a wider blast radius: it breaks LOCAL 'import parrot.security' (and every downstream test), not only CI 'uv sync'. FEAT-562 M2/M7/M8 (TASK-3297/3299/3300) cannot be verified until navigator-session 1.0.0 is installable. Fix belongs to the navigator-session upgrade / resolver work, not FEAT-562. Evidence: 'from navigator_session.vault import KeyRing' -> ImportError; navigator_session.__version__ == 0.10.0; packages/ai-parrot/pyproject.toml:105 requires >=1.0.0.

payload.title: BasicAgent.__init__ unconditionally constructs GoogleGenAIClient regardless of llm=
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/bots/agent.py:114-116 does `from ..clients.google import GoogleGenAIClient` then `default_client = GoogleGenAIClient()` on EVERY BasicAgent construction, before checking self._llm_raw. So constructing BasicAgent(name=..., llm='anthropic:...') still imports and instantiates the Google client; when google-genai / the ai-parrot-client-google satellite is not importable, construction raises ImportError/instantiation error even though Google was never requested. The comment claims a lazy import to avoid module-scope provider imports (AC-3), but it is still unconditional at __init__ time. Fix: only construct the Google default client when it is actually the resolved provider (or lazily on first multimodal/TTS use). Discovered while wiring FEAT-586's hello-world (test_hello_world_snippet_executes had to inject a fake parrot.clients.google to construct BasicAgent).

payload.title: Shared ledger: capture the deferred `wikitoolkit-ledger-arangodb` follow-up — the issues.jsonl snapshot is last-writer-wins across machines
payload.body:
IDEA (for whoever picks this up): put the SDD work ledger in a shared space, e.g. ArangoDB, so every machine and worktree reads and writes ONE ledger.

The gap today. The ledger is shared only across worktrees on a single host. FEAT-566 put it at `<main_worktree>/.parrot/ledger/`, as a SQLite index plus a local events.jsonl. Across machines, the only shared copy is the committed `sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl`. `wikitoolkit ledger export`, which /sdd-done step 9.1 also runs, overwrites that file with the exporting machine's local view, and nothing ever imports the committed snapshot back into a local log. So any export from a machine whose log is behind silently drops other people's issues.

Evidence (2026-10-14). Across 249 historical versions of the snapshot, 279 distinct issues were recorded. Only 161 were present: 118 had been dropped, including 49 major and 8 critical. Snapshot commits swing by 90–160 lines between exports from different machines and agents (Jesus, Jesus Lara, revbot, Arturo). They were restored from git history in a029275b9, and the loss will recur.

Prior decisions.
- FEAT-569 (wikitoolkit-http-mcp) deferred "Porting LedgerStore to ArangoDB — follow-up feature `wikitoolkit-ledger-arangodb`". That follow-up was never captured as a brainstorm, spec or issue; this issue captures it.
- FEAT-566 kept the ledger SQLite-first and noted that alternative backends remain possible via BaseWikiStore.

Building blocks that already exist.
- `knowledge/wiki/arango_store.py`, an ArangoDB wiki store.
- The BaseWikiStore abstraction that LedgerStore extends.
- `wikitoolkit sync push|pull`, which already shares memories and notes through a shared ENV plane. The ledger is excluded today.

Options.
1. Long term: port LedgerStore to ArangoDB (`wikitoolkit-ledger-arangodb`). issues.jsonl then becomes a read-only export, no longer the cross-machine source of truth.
2. Interim: point teams at FEAT-569's remote wikitoolkit server, whose server-side ledger is shared.
3. Short-term guard: make export merge with the committed snapshot by issue_id (newest state wins), and refuse to remove issues unless `--allow-removals` is passed.

Suggested next step: `/sdd-brainstorm wikitoolkit-ledger-arangodb` with Jesus. Until then, never commit `ledger export` output without diffing issues.jsonl.

payload.title: FEAT-705 migration advice silently drops the Prometheus metrics destination
payload.body: Spec line 515 recommends keeping Prometheus in OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT for traces-only OpenLIT routing, but the proposed metrics implementation reuses config.otlp_targets or the implicit endpoint. With OTLP_TARGETS=[OpenLIT], Prometheus is ignored for metrics. Current docs/architecture/10-observability.md lines 81-88 recommend this existing split configuration. Explicitly document this breaking routing change and a supported migration such as collector-side signal routing, or revise target semantics; remove the incorrect recommendation and add a mixed endpoint/target regression test.

payload.title: FEAT-705 reader-count tests inspect a process-wide SDK registry
payload.body: Spec line 329 instructs asserting len(provider._all_metric_readers)==2, and lines 434/451 describe this as the provider reader list. In installed OTel SDK this is a class-wide WeakSet shared by all MeterProvider instances; the provider-specific sequence is _metric_readers. A local probe created two providers with one reader each: both reported two global readers and one local reader, even after shutdown. Existing conftest resets API latches but not this registry. Use the provider-local sequence with a guarded private-attribute assertion or capture constructor arguments; cover multiple live providers so tests cannot count unrelated readers. Probe evidence: artifacts/logs/feat705_review_probes.log.

payload.title: Review TASK-4491
navigator-session 1.0 (KeyRing) mismatch breaks parrot.security import — root cause of FEAT-562 M7 DatabaseAgent test errors + the §1 resolver blocker
payload.body: FEAT-562 TASK-3299 (M7) diagnosis: the DatabaseAgent/botmanager 'cannot import name DatabaseAgentToolkit' CI errors are NOT an independent bug. Real cause: parrot.security.credentials_utils imports 'KeyRing, VaultContext, open_sealed, seal' from navigator_session.vault (added by the vault-crypto-hardening feature, commit cd8690390 which pinned navigator-session>=1.0.0), but the resolvable/installed navigator_session is 0.10.0, which has no KeyRing. So 'import parrot.security' raises ImportError, cascading through parrot.tools -> parrot.bots.database -> the DatabaseAgent tests. This is the SAME external resolver blocker recorded in the FEAT-562 spec §1 addendum (navigator-session>=1.0.0 unresolvable on py3.13), but with a wider blast radius: it breaks LOCAL 'import parrot.security' (and every downstream test), not only CI 'uv sync'. FEAT-562 M2/M7/M8 (TASK-3297/3299/3300) cannot be verified until navigator-session 1.0.0 is installable. Fix belongs to the navigator-session upgrade / resolver work, not FEAT-562. Evidence: 'from navigator_session.vault import KeyRing' -> ImportError; navigator_session.__version__ == 0.10.0; packages/ai-parrot/pyproject.toml:105 requires >=1.0.0.

payload.reason: Resolved: dev pins navigator-session>=1.0.1 (locked 1.0.1) + parrot 1.0.4; KeyRing imports; test-core green. The DatabaseAgent-import symptom this issue tracked is gone.

payload.title: Installer scripts carry an internal FEAT-586 breadcrumb comment
payload.body: Code-reviewer finding (SUGGESTION) during FEAT-586 review: scripts/install/install-parrot.sh:2 and install-parrot.ps1:3 both carry an explicit '(FEAT-586)' comment referencing the internal feature-tracking ID. AC14 is worded around 'the document' (docs/getting-started.md), which is clean, but these two scripts are also public-facing artifacts a PyPI user would run. A ticket-ID breadcrumb in a code comment is low risk and arguably fine as maintainer metadata (consistent with the rest of the codebase's FEAT-<NNN> comment convention), but if the intent of AC14/AC15 extends to 'no organization-specific content in anything public-facing', these two lines are the one place it leaks. Suggested fix: drop the '(FEAT-586)' parenthetical from both script header comments, or replace with a neutral description.

payload.title: install-guide CI job omits an explicit uv sync, unlike sibling jobs
payload.body: Code-reviewer finding (SUGGESTION) during FEAT-586 review: the install-guide job in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs 'uv run pytest packages/ai-parrot/tests/docs/ -q' with no preceding explicit 'uv sync ...' step, unlike every other job in the file (lint-and-registry, test-core, test-wiki-extras all sync explicitly before uv run). This is a deliberate choice — the doc-claim tests are written to tolerate a bare/no-satellite install (fallback to declared-provider-keys in test_named_providers_are_registered, fake-module injection in test_hello_world_snippet_executes) — and uv run implicitly syncs, so the job works. Suggested fix: add a one-line comment on the job noting the omission is intentional (proves the guide's own zero-providers warning), so it doesn't read as an oversight to the next maintainer.

payload.title: install-parrot.ps1 defaults -Python 'python', which may be absent if only the py launcher is on PATH
payload.body: Code-reviewer finding (NITPICK) during FEAT-586 review: on Windows, install-parrot.ps1 defaults -Python 'python' while the getting-started guide's own Windows venv-creation step recommends 'py -3.12' (the Python Launcher). If a reader only has the py launcher on PATH (no bare python.exe), the script's default would fail, and -Python can't be worked around by passing 'py -3.12' as a single value since it is invoked as one token (& $Python -m venv ...). Likely fine in practice (winget's python.org package typically also puts python.exe on PATH); no spec requirement or test covers this combination. Flagged as a minor real-world edge case, not a spec breach.

payload.title: BasicAgent.__init__ unconditionally constructs GoogleGenAIClient regardless of llm=
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/bots/agent.py:114-116 does `from ..clients.google import GoogleGenAIClient` then `default_client = GoogleGenAIClient()` on EVERY BasicAgent construction, before checking self._llm_raw. So constructing BasicAgent(name=..., llm='anthropic:...') still imports and instantiates the Google client; when google-genai / the ai-parrot-client-google satellite is not importable, construction raises ImportError/instantiation error even though Google was never requested. The comment claims a lazy import to avoid module-scope provider imports (AC-3), but it is still unconditional at __init__ time. Fix: only construct the Google default client when it is actually the resolved provider (or lazily on first multimodal/TTS use). Discovered while wiring FEAT-586's hello-world (test_hello_world_snippet_executes had to inject a fake parrot.clients.google to construct BasicAgent).

payload.title: examples/basic_agent.py unpacks invoke() as a 2-tuple; invoke() returns a single AIMessage
payload.body: examples/basic_agent.py:7 does `answer, response = await agent.invoke(question)`, but BaseBot.invoke() (packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/bots/base.py:628, return annotation -> AIMessage at line 638, returns AIMessage(...) at line 703) returns a SINGLE AIMessage, not a 2-tuple. Running the example raises ValueError (cannot unpack). The example is stale relative to the current invoke() contract and misleads new users following it verbatim. Fix: update the example to `answer = await agent.invoke(question); print(answer.output)` (or the current accessor). Discovered while deriving FEAT-586's hello-world from this example; the guide's docs/getting-started.md deliberately deviates to work around it.

payload.body:
What: packages/ai-parrot/tests/flows/dev_loop/test_subagent_parity.py::test_prompt_parity[sdd-worker] fails on dev (1 failed, 9 passed). The two copies of the sdd-worker prompt differ on the frontmatter `tools:` line (line 26): `.claude/agents/sdd-worker.md` lists `Monitor, TaskStop`; `packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/flows/dev_loop/_subagent_data/sdd-worker.md` does not.

Where it came from: commit bfe9acac0 (2026-10-08, "chore(agents): allow Monitor and TaskStop tools for sdd-worker") updated only the `.claude` copy, not its `_subagent_data` twin.

Why it matters: the parity test exists to keep the two copies identical, but CI does not run `packages/ai-parrot/tests/flows/dev_loop/`, so the regression went unnoticed. Runtime impact is low today (load_subagent_definition strips frontmatter), but the drift pattern will repeat. FEAT-633 (parrot-installer) adds a third copy under `parrot/sdd/_assets/`.

Suggested fix: (1) immediate: add `Monitor, TaskStop` to the `_subagent_data/sdd-worker.md` tools line so the test is green again; (2) durable: FEAT-633 amendment C2 (sdd/proposals/parrot-installer-amendments.proposal.md) — one canonical copy loaded from the packaged assets, removing the `_subagent_data` twins; and run this test (or the asset sync check) in CI.

payload.title: Shared ledger: capture the deferred `wikitoolkit-ledger-arangodb` follow-up — the issues.jsonl snapshot is last-writer-wins across machines
payload.body:
IDEA (for whoever picks this up): put the SDD work ledger in a shared space, e.g. ArangoDB, so every machine and worktree reads and writes ONE ledger.

The gap today. The ledger is shared only across worktrees on a single host. FEAT-566 put it at `<main_worktree>/.parrot/ledger/`, as a SQLite index plus a local events.jsonl. Across machines, the only shared copy is the committed `sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl`. `wikitoolkit ledger export`, which /sdd-done step 9.1 also runs, overwrites that file with the exporting machine's local view, and nothing ever imports the committed snapshot back into a local log. So any export from a machine whose log is behind silently drops other people's issues.

Evidence (2026-10-14). Across 249 historical versions of the snapshot, 279 distinct issues were recorded. Only 161 were present: 118 had been dropped, including 49 major and 8 critical. Snapshot commits swing by 90–160 lines between exports from different machines and agents (Jesus, Jesus Lara, revbot, Arturo). They were restored from git history in a029275b9, and the loss will recur.

Prior decisions.
- FEAT-569 (wikitoolkit-http-mcp) deferred "Porting LedgerStore to ArangoDB — follow-up feature `wikitoolkit-ledger-arangodb`". That follow-up was never captured as a brainstorm, spec or issue; this issue captures it.
- FEAT-566 kept the ledger SQLite-first and noted that alternative backends remain possible via BaseWikiStore.

Building blocks that already exist.
- `knowledge/wiki/arango_store.py`, an ArangoDB wiki store.
- The BaseWikiStore abstraction that LedgerStore extends.
- `wikitoolkit sync push|pull`, which already shares memories and notes through a shared ENV plane. The ledger is excluded today.

Options.
1. Long term: port LedgerStore to ArangoDB (`wikitoolkit-ledger-arangodb`). issues.jsonl then becomes a read-only export, no longer the cross-machine source of truth.
2. Interim: point teams at FEAT-569's remote wikitoolkit server, whose server-side ledger is shared.
3. Short-term guard: make export merge with the committed snapshot by issue_id (newest state wins), and refuse to remove issues unless `--allow-removals` is passed.

Suggested next step: `/sdd-brainstorm wikitoolkit-ledger-arangodb` with Jesus. Until then, never commit `ledger export` output without diffing issues.jsonl.

payload.title: Review TASK-4478
semantic usage rights block granted metrics (spec AC6 scopes them to masked/hidden columns)
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot-semantic/src/parrot/semantic/governance/lineage.py enforce_usage_rights requires a usage grant for EVERY non-projection physical-column use, including the aggregate input of a granted metric (SUM(sales.orders.amount) is context 'derived'). An analyst granted metric 'revenue' gets usage_denied on sales.orders.amount; usage lists cannot name 'amount' because policy validation only accepts member names (unknown_member), so only usage:"*" works. Spec §3 M6 / AC6 scope usage rights to 'masked or hidden' columns, but 'hidden' is undefined and ModelMember has no member->physical-column mapping. Needs a design decision (e.g. define hidden = backs a member not granted to the role / sensitive=True, exempt trusted compiler metric-definition nodes). Repro: tests/test_e2e_governed.py::test_e2e_granted_metric_requires_no_usage_grant (xfail strict). Blocks normal non-admin use of FEAT-704.

payload.title: sl_run_sql can project columns of members not granted to the role
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot-semantic/src/parrot/semantic/toolkit.py run_sql governs raw SQL with GovernancePipeline only (per spec AC12). The pipeline authorizes tables (PBAC), masks masked columns and enforces usage rights on masked/sensitive columns (decision A), but nothing checks PROJECTED columns against the role's member grants (RoleCatalog.check_query_rights only runs on the structured path). With allow_raw_sql=True an analyst can `SELECT tenant_id FROM sales.orders` (unmasked, not granted) and receive it. Opt-in feature (default off), but it contradicts the per-role member allowlist. Suggested fix: in the pipeline or run_sql, map projected physical columns to members and deny projection of non-granted members (or require a mask/sensitive flag for every non-granted column); add a run_sql e2e case.

payload.title: semantic toolkit: catalog/minor hardening follow-ups from FEAT-704 review
payload.body:
FEAT-704 code-review suggestions, verified in code, deferred:
S1 toolkit.py list_models/search_data_model raise on the first denied model instead of filtering to visible ones (fails closed, bad UX with partial grants).
S2 engines/__init__.py calls cache.put(compiled) without model_digest, so CompileCache.invalidate_model is a no-op (correct only because the digest is in the key).
S3 toolkit.py _pre_execute falls back to static_subject whenever _permission_context is missing; in server deployments it should only apply on the mcp-local channel.
S4 governance/pbac.py PbacGate.available probes find_spec('navigator_auth') at top level; core's fail-open branch triggers on submodule ImportError — probe the exact module.
S5 toolkit.py save_result_as_dataset re-checks only that some member is visible; check the handle's own members against the role grants.
Nits: trusted_nodes relies on id() of nodes (hold strong refs/flag nodes); LoadedModel.schema shadows a BaseModel attribute; redundant expires_at=now() at ResultHandle call sites; handlers/semantic.py logger.exception outside an except (ruff LOG004).

payload.title: Review TASK-4478
semantic usage rights block granted metrics (spec AC6 scopes them to masked/hidden columns)
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot-semantic/src/parrot/semantic/governance/lineage.py enforce_usage_rights requires a usage grant for EVERY non-projection physical-column use, including the aggregate input of a granted metric (SUM(sales.orders.amount) is context 'derived'). An analyst granted metric 'revenue' gets usage_denied on sales.orders.amount; usage lists cannot name 'amount' because policy validation only accepts member names (unknown_member), so only usage:"*" works. Spec §3 M6 / AC6 scope usage rights to 'masked or hidden' columns, but 'hidden' is undefined and ModelMember has no member->physical-column mapping. Needs a design decision (e.g. define hidden = backs a member not granted to the role / sensitive=True, exempt trusted compiler metric-definition nodes). Repro: tests/test_e2e_governed.py::test_e2e_granted_metric_requires_no_usage_grant (xfail strict). Blocks normal non-admin use of FEAT-704.

payload.title: sl_run_sql can project columns of members not granted to the role
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot-semantic/src/parrot/semantic/toolkit.py run_sql governs raw SQL with GovernancePipeline only (per spec AC12). The pipeline authorizes tables (PBAC), masks masked columns and enforces usage rights on masked/sensitive columns (decision A), but nothing checks PROJECTED columns against the role's member grants (RoleCatalog.check_query_rights only runs on the structured path). With allow_raw_sql=True an analyst can `SELECT tenant_id FROM sales.orders` (unmasked, not granted) and receive it. Opt-in feature (default off), but it contradicts the per-role member allowlist. Suggested fix: in the pipeline or run_sql, map projected physical columns to members and deny projection of non-granted members (or require a mask/sensitive flag for every non-granted column); add a run_sql e2e case.

payload.body: packages/ai-parrot-semantic/src/parrot/semantic/loader.py builds one PhysicalSchema and member list for the whole sidemantic layer and attaches them to every LoadedModel. With allow_raw_sql=True and two policy files, sl_run_sql(model="A", sql=<tables of B>) passes the positive guard and PBAC (the manifest covers every layer table) while only A's RLS/masks apply. Fix: scope PhysicalSchema/members per policy model (its table plus join-reachable tables), or reject tables not owned by the named model.
